ledger.claim: The measured excess on this trip is established and substantial. The gps_trace records 29.98 km against a booked optimal route of 24.0 km — an excess of 5.98 km, or 24.9% of optimal_distance_km. Both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test pass: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence.

trip_record.actual_distance_km (30.0 km) is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may NOT be cited for the threshold test; gps_trace.trace_distance_km (29.98 km) is the governing field. The trace is also unimpaired for policy purposes: 229 fixes at a 10 second sampling interval across 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires and the excess stands exactly as measured without any independent corroboration being required.

The route is independently corroborated by the driver's own words. His chat message at 07:54:20 reads 'boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok' — an admission that he left the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang. A driver admission in the chat log is one of the independent sources POL-RD-07(ii) names, so the 5.98 km excess does not rest on the telemetry alone.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00111 and the same 07:47:40 pickup event, and limb (b) — an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold — is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden has therefore shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause if he is to excuse the deviation.

The rider's profile does not gate this claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so the additional-corroboration requirement never engages and the 24.9% excess needs no support beyond the gps_trace — which it has in any event from the driver's chat admission.

No exoneration arises under POL-RD-04. The only rider message in the chat log is 'as long as i reach by 8.30' at 07:54:55. It names no road, its waypoint_hint is null, and it is not an instruction specific enough to act on, so the corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable. The detour was the driver's own routing decision, not a rider request.

The closure defence is not made out on the record. POL-RD-03(c) requires the actual route to leave the optimal corridor before the affected segment AND rejoin IT after. This trip's recorded optimal route is 'BKE southbound then PIE westbound', while the trace summary describes the rejoin as being made 'on the AYE'. Nothing in the trip record, the trace summary or the advisory places that rejoin on the booked optimal corridor, so limb (c) is unmet and the excess is not exonerated.

If the closure defence fails, the refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. On the booked optimal route the recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 31.00. Charged_total is 37.74 and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the refund is 37.74 - 31.00 = 6.74, rounded up to SGD 6.75 — a PARTIAL_REFUND above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share.

The threshold test under POL-RD-01 is met only narrowly and the deviation is NOT material. The governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, 29.98 km, not the rounded 30.0 km on the trip record. Against the booked optimal of 24.0 km that is an excess of 5.98 km and 24.92%, which clears the 0.8 km / 20% establishment tests but falls short of both materiality thresholds (8.0 km and 50%). The POL-RD-06 conduct check is therefore not engaged by this trip.

The LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260803-014 is a CLOSURE on the Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after the Clementi Rd exit. The booked optimal route recorded on the trip record is BKE southbound then PIE westbound, so the advisory names the very expressway segment the optimal route traverses; the advisory payload records intersects_route as true. This satisfies POL-RD-03(a).

The advisory's validity window, 07:10 to 09:30, brackets the whole trip window of 07:47:40 to 08:25:40, with an overlap of 41.5 minutes. That is far inside the 15-minute buffer POL-RD-03(b) allows at each end, and the advisory was issued before the trip began, so it is not an after-the-fact reconstruction of the traffic.

The GPS trace matches the closure to an actual route diversion. The driver came off the corridor at Bukit Panjang, before the closed Clementi Rd to Jalan Anak Bukit segment, and rejoined after it via Upper Bukit Timah and the AYE — the diversion the advisory itself describes. That is the leave-before / rejoin-after pattern POL-RD-03(c) requires, and the trace is unbroken at 100% coverage with zero gaps.

The exoneration cap does not bite here. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(measured excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 7.76) = 5.98 km. The measured excess of 5.98 km is entirely within the 7.76 km cap, so the whole of the diversion is exonerated and no excess remains to be refunded.

Running the POL-RD-02 arithmetic against the closure-adjusted optimal route (24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, duration 37.5 minutes, the booked 30.0 minutes scaled by the distance ratio) gives a recomputed fare of 37.585 SGD against a charged total of 37.74 SGD — a residual of 0.155 SGD. That is below the 0.50 SGD de-minimis threshold, so the only lawful outcome is NO_ACTION: the charge stands as charged, and the rider's claim for the disputed 8.00 SGD is not supported.

There is no separate ERP or toll correction to add. The fare breakdown shows tolls_erp of 0.00 and an empty erp_gantries list — neither the optimal route nor the route driven crosses a gantry at this hour — so the POL-RD-09(2) pass-through correction for an externally-caused closure computes to zero and adds nothing to the rider's recovery.

The driver gave the rider contemporaneous notice before diverting and the rider did not object. At 07:54:20 the driver messaged 'boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok', and the rider's only reply at 07:54:55 was 'as long as i reach by 8.30'. The rider neither requested a different road nor disputed the diversion at the time, which corroborates the POL-RD-03 account rather than contradicting it.

No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 229 fixes over 2,280 seconds at a 10-second sample interval (well under the 30-second limb), a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, and no jumps — so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are all unmet and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. Trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and no refund approaches SGD 150.00 or charged_total.

POL-RD-06 is not engaged because the deviation is not material, and in any event no repeat-deviation pattern could be established: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 588 completed_trips_90d, which is below the count of 3 and the 0.05 ratio the clause requires. There is nothing on this driver's trailing-window record to aggravate the trip.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — trip TRP-00111, Woodlands to one-north, 3 Aug 2026.

The route deviation is established, but it is not material, and it is fully exonerated by the LTA closure, so the rider's claim is not supported and the charge stands.

Deviation. The governing distance is the GPS trace figure of 29.98 km, not the rounded 30.0 km on the trip record (POL-RD-01: trip_record.actual_distance_km is a convenience copy). Against the booked optimal of 24.0 km that is an excess of 5.98 km, or 24.9%, which passes the 20% and 0.8 km establishment tests but stays below both materiality thresholds (50% / 8.0 km). The POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation check is therefore not engaged, and the driver's trailing-90-day record (0 flags over 588 completed trips) shows no pattern in any event.

Exoneration. Advisory ADV-20260803-014 is a HIGH-severity closure on the PIE towards Tuas between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit — precisely the segment the booked optimal route (BKE southbound then PIE westbound) traverses. Its geometry intersects the route and its 07:10–09:30 window brackets the 07:47:40–08:25:40 trip with 41.5 minutes of overlap, satisfying POL-RD-03(a) and (b). The trace shows the driver leaving the corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed stretch and rejoining it after, via Upper Bukit Timah Road and the AYE — the diversion the LTA advisory itself directs.

I do not accept the rider's argument that POL-RD-03(c) fails because the rejoin was 'on the AYE' rather than the booked PIE. Limb (c) asks whether the actual route left the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoined it after. The trace did exactly that: it left the BKE at Bukit Panjang, ahead of the closed PIE stretch, and rejoined the route beyond it on the AYE, the alternative the advisory names. The trace's own record describes the 'rejoin', and the closure clause's own example — 'a PIE closure at the Jalan Anak Bukit exit' — is this case. Limb (c) is met.

Cap and arithmetic. The POL-RD-03 cap is min(measured_excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 7.76) = 5.98 km, so the whole measured excess is justified and nothing is left to refund for the detour. The closure-adjusted optimal route is 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km over a scaled 37.5 minutes. Recomputing under POL-RD-02 against that adjusted route: (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 37.585. The charged total was 37.74, so the residual is 0.155 — below the 0.50 de-minimis threshold. No refund issues. For completeness, the rider's alternative figure (recomputed fare 31.00 against the booked route, refund 6.74 rounded up to 6.75) is the arithmetic that would follow only if the closure defence failed; it does not fail, so that figure does not govern.

Other clauses. The driver's in-app message and the rider's reply are consistent with the closure account (he announced the diversion before making it and the rider did not object), but the message is not a rider instruction under POL-RD-04 — it names no road, its waypoint_hint is null, and 'as long as i reach by 8.30' is not specific enough to act on — so POL-RD-04 adds no separate exoneration, and none is needed. There is no ERP or toll correction: tolls_erp is 0.00 and erp_gantries is empty, so POL-RD-09 settles nothing and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises. The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (229 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps), so POL-RD-07 is not engaged and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. Payment status and refund_issued_sgd are left unchanged: the charge of 37.74 stands.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
